# 配置项

Spring Boot 宿主读取的 `wow.*` 配置的全部键，共 226 个，由宿主的配置元数据（[`spring-configuration-metadata.json`](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/Wow/blob/v10/host/spring-boot/src/main/resources/META-INF/spring-configuration-metadata.json)）生成；说明取自源码，为英文。Spring Boot 按宽松规则绑定：`max-concurrent`、`maxConcurrent` 与 `MAX_CONCURRENT` 是同一个键。没有任何属性对应的 `wow.*` 键会在节点启动时报告。映射之下的键，若映射的键含点，要放进方括号：`wow.aggregates.[shop.cart].tenant`。

## `wow`

| 键 | 类型 | 默认值 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `wow.aggregates` | `Map<String,Aggregate>` |  | Per aggregate type, by `<context>.<aggregate>` (bracketed in a property name: `wow.aggregates.[shop.cart]`). |
| `wow.backend` | `String` | `auto` | The backend of a node that names no `wow.stores`: `auto` (the default) takes PostgreSQL or MongoDB by the application's `DataSource` or `MongoClient`, and refuses to start without either unless a profile of `wow.internal.dev-profiles` is active or the internal port binds the loopback interface alone; `memory` keeps the data in memory on purpose, for one node whose data does not outlive it. |
| `wow.ddl` | `StoreDdl` | `auto` | How the stores manage the framework's tables, collections and indexes: `auto` creates what is missing (the default), `validate` creates nothing and refuses a store whose schema is missing or in another format, `none` creates and checks nothing; `wow.stores.<name>.ddl` overrides it for one store. |
| `wow.schedules` | `Map<String,Schedule>` |  | Per `@OnSchedule` job, by its name: `wow.schedules.<job>.*`. |
| `wow.service` | `String` |  | The service's name; `spring.application.name` when not set. |
| `wow.stores` | `Map<String,Store>` |  | The named store instances, by name: `wow.stores.<name>.type` and its settings. |
| `wow.subscriptions` | `Map<String,SubscriptionSettings>` |  | Per subscription, by its name (bracketed in a property name: `wow.subscriptions.[CartSaga.onOrderCreated]`). |

## `wow.calls`

The synchronous calls of the node's sagas to the command gateways of other contexts: each context's base URL (contexts, `wow.calls.contexts.<context>.url`: the target's internal port, `http://host:port` of an address in its internal network, never its public port, which refuses calls), the service token the node presents as `Authorization: Bearer` (token; an application's me.ahoo.wow.client.ServiceCredential bean, such as one that renews a CoSec token, replaces it), how long one call may take (timeout) and connect (connectTimeout). A saga that calls a context without a URL fails, then parks.

| 键 | 类型 | 默认值 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `wow.calls.connect-timeout` | `Duration` | `PT2S` |  |
| `wow.calls.contexts` | `Map<String,CallTarget>` |  |  |
| `wow.calls.timeout` | `Duration` | `PT10S` |  |
| `wow.calls.token` | `String` |  |  |

## `wow.clickhouse`

ClickHouse's configuration, `wow.clickhouse.*`, read when wow-clickhouse is on the classpath (ClickHouseAutoConfiguration): - `wow.clickhouse.endpoint`: the server's HTTP endpoint, such as `http://localhost:8123`; ClickHouse is wired only when it is set. `username` (`default`) and `password` (empty) sign in; `database` (`default`) holds the tables. - `wow.clickhouse.sink.enabled`: whether the Manifest's published streams are written to ClickHouse; on by default. - `wow.clickhouse.sink.ddl`: `auto` (create what is missing, then validate; the default), `validate` or `none`. - `wow.clickhouse.sink.batch-size`: the most records one insert carries (1000). - `wow.clickhouse.sink.deduplication-window`: how many recent inserts each table remembers to drop a retried one (1000), the `non_replicated_deduplication_window` of the tables `auto` creates. - `wow.clickhouse.sink.aggregates.<context>.<aggregate>.history.enabled`: whether every commit is kept (on by default); off keeps only the current state. `...history.ttl`: how long the history is kept, forever when unset. - `wow.clickhouse.query.enabled`: whether the datasets are served from ClickHouse; on by default. - `wow.clickhouse.query.metadata-ttl`: how long a dataset table's columns and engine are reused before `system.columns` is read again (1m). - `wow.clickhouse.query.settings.<name>`: server settings every dataset query runs under, such as `max_memory_usage`; the execution time comes from each query's budget (`wow.query.http.timeout`), not from here.

| 键 | 类型 | 默认值 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `wow.clickhouse.database` | `String` | `default` |  |
| `wow.clickhouse.endpoint` | `String` |  |  |
| `wow.clickhouse.password` | `String` | `""` |  |
| `wow.clickhouse.username` | `String` | `default` |  |

## `wow.clients`

The typed clients of the peer contexts over HTTP, `wow-client`'s: a peer context listed in contexts is reached over HTTP by the service's me.ahoo.wow.api.client.CommandClient and me.ahoo.wow.api.read.QueryApi beans, in its ClientTarget.mode (or mode); any other context as without these clients. Where each is: its public routes' base ClientTarget.url (user mode) and its internal port's ClientTarget.internalUrl (service mode; `wow.calls.contexts.<context>.url` when not set, which the sagas' calls use too), or what an application's me.ahoo.wow.client.EndpointResolver bean resolves. Each request is answered within timeout (a command's longer wait aside) after connecting within connectTimeout, and retried as retry says; a user-mode request forwards the forwardedHeaders of the public request it serves. The service mode presents the me.ahoo.wow.client.ServiceCredential bean (`wow.calls.token`).

| 键 | 类型 | 默认值 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `wow.clients.connect-timeout` | `Duration` | `PT2S` |  |
| `wow.clients.contexts` | `Map<String,ClientTarget>` |  |  |
| `wow.clients.forwarded-headers` | `List<String>` | `Authorization` |  |
| `wow.clients.mode` | `Mode` | `service` |  |
| `wow.clients.timeout` | `Duration` | `PT30S` |  |

## `wow.internal`

| 键 | 类型 | 默认值 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `wow.internal.connect-timeout` | `Duration` | `PT1S` | How long a peer has to accept a connection of the cluster channel or the signal sender. |
| `wow.internal.dev-profiles` | `Set<String>` | `dev, local, test, demo` | The development profiles, `dev`, `local`, `test` and `demo`: in them the internal port may run without token, and `wow.backend=auto` falls back to memory when no durable backend is available. |
| `wow.internal.host` | `String` |  | The address the internal server binds, `0.0.0.0` for every interface; when not set, the host of the member address the node advertises (`wow.node.address`, else this host's address). |
| `wow.internal.port` | `Integer` | `9090` | The port of the internal server: the cluster channel and the wait signals; 0 for one the system chooses, which the node advertises once the server is bound. |
| `wow.internal.signal-queue-capacity` | `Integer` | `1024` | The signals queued per origin node before they are dropped. |
| `wow.internal.token` | `List<String>` |  | The service's cluster tokens, at least 32 characters each: the secret its nodes share, which alone opens the cluster channel (`/wow/internal/forward`) and the wait signals of the internal port. A node sends the first and takes any, so a token is rotated by adding the new one second, then moving it first on every node, then removing the old one; a comma-separated value (`WOW_INTERNAL_TOKEN`) is a list. A service token of `wow.http.services` opens the call routes, not these, and this token no call route. A node without one starts only in a profile of devProfiles, or with its internal port bound to the loopback interface alone, and warns: its cluster routes then take every request. |

## `wow.kafka`

The Kafka transport's configuration, `wow.kafka.*`, read when wow-kafka is on the classpath (KafkaAutoConfiguration): - `wow.kafka.bootstrap-servers`: the brokers; the transport, the Kafka Sink and the Kafka-sourced subscriptions are wired only when it is set. - `wow.kafka.properties.*`: passed to every producer and consumer as they are (`security.protocol`, `client.id`, `linger.ms`,...), except the settings the transport's guarantees rest on (`me.ahoo.wow.kafka.KafkaOptions`). - `wow.kafka.topic-prefix`: put before every topic name, such as `staging.` for `staging.wow.shop.order.state`; none by default, so the topics are the Manifest's. The sinks write under it and the subscriptions of other contexts' streams read under it. - `wow.kafka.poll-timeout`: the longest a consumer's poll waits (200 ms by default); a read that is cancelled, and a partition that joins or leaves a topic's shared consumer, take effect within it. - `wow.kafka.offset-gap`: what a read of another context's topic does when its partition no longer holds the offset it is to read from (the retention deleted it, or the topic was created again): `fail` (the default) fails the read, so the subscription stays where it is, logging errors, until an operator moves its checkpoint; `earliest` reads on from the earliest offset retained. Either way the gap is logged as an error and counted (`wow.kafka.offset.gaps`). - `wow.kafka.command-intake`: whether each context the node hosts executes the commands other contexts send to its command topic, `wow.<context>.commands`; off by default. The topic must exist with as many partitions as the context's log, and the node checks it at start. Sending commands to other contexts and reading their receipts need no switch. A context with an aggregate type routed through Kafka takes them whatever this says. - `wow.kafka.topics.ddl`: how the node manages the topics its contexts own at its start, see Topics: `validate` (the default) fails the start when one is missing or a command topic does not have exactly `wow.log.partitions` partitions; `auto` creates the missing ones first; `none` checks only the command topics the node reads, whose partitions must still be the log's. - `wow.kafka.topics.replication-factor` (the broker's default), `wow.kafka.topics.min-insync-replicas` (the broker's default) and `wow.kafka.topics.configs.*` (`retention.ms`,...): what `auto` creates a topic with. A command accepted on a command topic is durable only when both are at least 2: at start the node warns when they are below that, as configured or as the command topics of its contexts are, unless a profile of Topics.devProfiles is active (`dev`, `local`, `test`, `demo`). - `wow.kafka.topics.partition-refresh` (30s): how often the node looks for partitions added to the topics it reads (other contexts' streams, its receipts), and its consumers' `metadata.max.age.ms`; the new partitions are read within about twice this.

| 键 | 类型 | 默认值 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `wow.kafka.bootstrap-servers` | `String` |  |  |
| `wow.kafka.command-intake` | `Boolean` | `false` |  |
| `wow.kafka.offset-gap` | `OffsetGapPolicy` | `fail` |  |
| `wow.kafka.poll-timeout` | `Duration` | `PT0.2S` |  |
| `wow.kafka.properties` | `Map<String,String>` |  |  |
| `wow.kafka.topic-prefix` | `String` | `""` |  |

## `wow.query`

The query plane's configuration, `wow.query.*`, read by QueryAutoConfiguration: - `wow.query.enabled` (true): whether the query routes and gateways are wired at all. - `wow.query.http.*`: the HTTP budget (QueryBudget) every query route runs under: `max-list-size` (1000), `max-page-size` (100), `max-page-window` (10000), `max-filter-nodes` (128), `max-filter-values` (1000), `allow-expensive-operators` (true), `max-residual-groups` (10000), `count-limit`, `allow-exact-count` (false), `timeout` (30s), `unindexed-sort-expensive` (false); and `default-list-size` (100), the limit of a list that names none. A limit of `0` is off. - `wow.query.in-process.*`: the budget of in-process queries, the typed me.ahoo.wow.api.read.QueryApi's, of trusted code too: the same keys and defaults as `wow.query.http.*`, its `default-list-size` the limit of an in-process list that names none. - `wow.query.in-process-timeout` (30s): the timeout of an in-process query that has no budget, trusted code's that dropped it (`QueryApi.trusted().unbounded()`). - `wow.query.require-explicit-entry`, `wow.query.require-authenticated-scope` (both false): the entry gates. - `wow.query.abac.*`: `enabled` (false), `require-principal-tags` (false), `match-missing-tag-key` (true), `attribute-prefix` (`abac.`): the caller's `abac.<key>` attributes matched against the snapshots' `tags`. - `wow.query.sensitivity.display-comparable` (true): whether filters and sorts may compare a `DISPLAY` value. - `wow.query.index.ddl`: how the snapshot backend manages the indexes of each aggregate's `x-wow-index` at startup. - `wow.query.count-cache.*`: `enabled` (true), `max-entries` (10000), `ttl` (30s): the cache of the snapshot counts and paged totals, valid while the type's snapshot write checkpoint holds and for at most `ttl`; `events-enabled` caches the events' counts the same way, though the log runs ahead of that checkpoint, so a cached events count may lag the streams for up to `ttl`. - `wow.query.dataset.config-directory`: the working directory whose `wow/dataset/` holds dataset files, `{context}.{dataset}.json`; each takes precedence over the classpath's `META-INF/wow/dataset/` file of the same dataset. The datasets of both are served when a dataset backend is wired (ClickHouse's, say). - `wow.query.memory.enabled`: whether the snapshots on a store in memory are queried, from the in-memory reference query backend, and the events of a log in memory, scanned in memory: for local runs, demos and tests, not for production. - `wow.query.events.*`: the `events` model, served from each aggregate's log store, or the store its `wow.aggregates.[<context>.<aggregate>].query.events.store` names: `mongo-read-preference` (none, the primary), the MongoDB read preference of its queries (`secondaryPreferred`, say), so a free filter scans a secondary rather than the primary the log appends to; `wow.stores.<name>.query.read-preference` takes its place for one store, and sets that of its snapshot queries too. `unpinned`: whether an events query that names no `aggregateId` runs, over which `wow.stores.<name>.query.events.unpinned` and `wow.aggregates.[<context>.<aggregate>].query.events.unpinned` decide for one store or aggregate type; refused, it is `wow.query.invalid` (`STORAGE_UNSUPPORTED` on `aggregateId`), and the model's descriptor lists the constraint `AGGREGATE_REQUIRED`. - `wow.query.dataset.max-concurrent`: how many dataset queries the node runs at once, under one bulkhead, `datasets`, which keeps the analytics queries from taking a warehouse the Sink writes to; `0` sets none. A query beyond it waits for `wow.query.dataset.max-wait` (`wow.query.max-wait` when unset) in a queue of `wow.query.dataset.max-queued` (`wow.query.max-queued`, else 4 per permit), then is `wow.query.busy`. The bound is fixed, not adaptive: the warehouse's writes (the ClickHouse Sink's) give the node no write pressure to adapt to. - `wow.query.max-concurrent`: how many snapshot and `events` queries each store runs at once, whichever entry asks, beyond which a query is `wow.query.busy` (429, with `Retry-After`); `wow.stores.<name>.query.max-concurrent` takes its place for one store; `0` for no bound. A query beyond the bound waits in a FIFO queue at most `wow.query.max-wait` (200ms) for a permit, and is refused when the wait runs out or when `wow.query.max-queued` (4 per permit) queries wait already; `wow.stores.<name>.query.max-wait` and `.max-queued` take their place for one store. - `wow.query.adaptive.*`: the bound of a store whose `max-concurrent` neither `wow.query.max-concurrent` nor `wow.stores.<name>.query.max-concurrent` fixes adapts to the store's write pressure, evaluated every `interval` (1s): `periods` (2) periods in a row in which its appends' p90 latency is above `latency-factor` (1.5) times its baseline and at least `min-latency` (5ms), or in which `connection-waits` (1) callers wait for a connection of its pool, halve it down to `floor` (1); a calm period in which a query waited or was refused raises it by one up to `ceiling` (none: the provider's, PostgreSQL half a pool the appends share, all of a `query-data-source`'s). `enabled` (true) turns it off; `wow.stores.<name>.query.adaptive.enabled`, `.floor` and `.ceiling` take their place for one store. - `wow.query.state.max-replay`: the most commits a state point read replays from the aggregate's snapshot, or from version 1 (`GET …/state?version=` or `?at=`, `…/state/trace`, the latest state before the first snapshot); a state further away is 400 `wow.query.invalid` (`REPLAY_TOO_LONG`). - `wow.query.stream.*`: a `list` streamed as server-sent events reads keyset chunks of `chunk-size` (500) records, a query permit per chunk, each record's `id` its position; after `max-hold` (30s; `0` for no bound) it ends with `end` `{"reason":"hold-expired","resumable":true}` and the client resumes it with `Last-Event-ID`. Neither `http.max-list-size` nor `http.default-list-size` bounds such a stream. A list whose sort cannot order a cursor streams without positions, under those bounds, and every `end` it sends (the hold time's included) says `"resumable":false`.

| 键 | 类型 | 默认值 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `wow.query.enabled` | `Boolean` | `true` |  |
| `wow.query.in-process-timeout` | `Duration` | `PT30S` |  |
| `wow.query.max-concurrent` | `Integer` |  |  |
| `wow.query.max-queued` | `Integer` |  |  |
| `wow.query.max-wait` | `Duration` | `PT0.2S` |  |
| `wow.query.require-authenticated-scope` | `Boolean` | `false` |  |
| `wow.query.require-explicit-entry` | `Boolean` | `false` |  |

| 键 | 类型 | 默认值 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `wow.wait.default-timeout` | `Duration` | `PT10S` | How long a command whose request names no timeout waits (`Wow-Wait-Timeout`), whichever edge it came through: at most maxTimeout. |
| `wow.wait.max-hops` | `Integer` | `16` | The most hops of a wait plan, at most WaitOptions.MAX_HOPS_CAP; each saga a chain follows adds two. |
| `wow.wait.max-registered` | `Integer` | `16384` | The most waits the node holds at once: beyond it a command whose plan waits past ACCEPTED is not run and is answered `wow.command.busy` (429, with `Retry-After`), FAILED at ACCEPTED. |
| `wow.wait.max-timeout` | `Duration` | `PT1M` | The longest wait; a longer timeout is capped to it, and a node stops within it. |
| `wow.wait.unknown-contexts` | `UnknownContexts` | `allow` | Whether a wait plan may name a context the node knows no Manifest of: `allow`, checked where the chain arrives, or `reject`. |
